questions.q: What is Ola Hallengren's Maintenance Solution, precisely?
options: A free, open-source set of T-SQL scripts (from ola.hallengren.com) that install stored procedures for backups, index maintenance, and integrity checks
A paid, licensed third-party product requiring a separate installer
A built-in SQL Server feature enabled by default on every instance
A cloud-only service exclusive to Azure SQL Database
questions.explain: It's free and open-source — you download and run a .sql script that creates stored procedures and Agent job shells using standard T-SQL.

questions.q: Which stored procedure from the solution applies fragmentation-aware REORGANIZE/REBUILD logic and statistics updates?
questions.explain: IndexOptimize implements the threshold-based reorganize-vs-rebuild decision from Lesson 34, plus statistics updates, across whatever databases/indexes are targeted.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what genuinely hard problem does the solution handle correctly that many hand-rolled scripts or Maintenance Plan configurations get wrong?
options: Encrypting backup files with Always Encrypted
questions.explain: The solution correctly runs maintenance per-partition on partitioned indexes rather than blindly rebuilding an entire massive index unnecessarily — a subtlety many custom scripts miss.

questions.q: What does the DatabaseIntegrityCheck procedure wrap?
questions.explain: DatabaseIntegrityCheck is the solution's wrapper around DBCC CHECKDB, with parameters for scope and PHYSICAL_ONLY behavior.

questions.q: In most real production environments, what is the relationship between Ola Hallengren's solution and hand-built SSMS Maintenance Plans (Lesson 33)?
options: The solution typically replaces hand-built Maintenance Plans entirely for these tasks
They are always run together, doubling up on the same tasks
Maintenance Plans are required first before installing the solution
The solution only works if no Maintenance Plan exists on the instance
questions.explain: Because it performs the same real operations with better execution quality (parameterization, partitioned-index handling, logging), it's typically installed in place of hand-built Maintenance Plans, not alongside them.
